evals.prompt: I created a DocumentProcessedEvent that implements IStructuredLogEvent and decorated it with [StructuredEvent("DocumentProcessedEvent")]. I registered it in my logger subclass with Register<DocumentProcessedEvent>(). When I call _logger.LogEvent(new DocumentProcessedEvent { ... }) nothing appears in Geneva. What could be wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the Geneva monitoring agent XML configuration must have a matching table entry and the agent must be redeployed — this is a separate step from DI/code registration. Confirms the code-side pattern is correct.
assertions: Identifies the Geneva monitoring agent XML configuration as the missing step
Explains that the agent must be redeployed after adding the table entry
Confirms the code-side pattern (sealed, IStructuredLogEvent, [StructuredEvent], Register<T>()) is correct

evals.prompt: I want to exclude calls to my /health endpoint from my availability SLO calculations. How do I do that with the LENS telemetry library?
evals.expected_output: Recommends implementing ISyntheticRequestDetector and registering it in DI before AddLensTelemetry. Shows an example checking the request path or route values. Does not suggest manually setting IsSynthetic in controller code.
assertions: Recommends implementing ISyntheticRequestDetector
Shows registration in DI before AddLensTelemetry
Does not suggest manually calling CoreRequestContextItems.IsSynthetic.SetItem() in the controller as the primary solution

evals.prompt: How do I mark a 401 response as meeting the reliability bar? My service intentionally returns 401 as part of an auth challenge flow and I don't want it counted as a reliability failure.
evals.expected_output: Recommends setting CoreRequestContextItems.ReliabilityScenario with a descriptive non-empty string value before returning the 401. Explains that a non-empty ReliabilityScenario causes MetReliabilityBar to be set to True regardless of HTTP status code.
assertions: Recommends CoreRequestContextItems.ReliabilityScenario.SetItem() with a descriptive string value
Explains that a non-empty ReliabilityScenario sets MetReliabilityBar to True regardless of status code

evals.prompt: I added the GenevaTelemetry config section to appsettings.json but omitted LongRequestThresholdMs. Now every single request is emitting an InboundQOSEvent. Why?
evals.expected_output: Explains that LongRequestThresholdMs defaults to 0 when omitted. The middleware emits InboundQOSEvent when latency > LongRequestThresholdMs, so a threshold of 0 means any request with measurable latency (which is every request) triggers the event. Recommends setting LongRequestThresholdMs to a meaningful value such as 1000 ms.
assertions: Identifies that LongRequestThresholdMs defaults to 0 when the key is absent
Explains that the emit condition is latency > LongRequestThresholdMs, so 0 causes every request to emit
Recommends setting LongRequestThresholdMs to a non-zero value (e.g. 1000)

evals.prompt: My service threw a 500 error. I have the correlationId from the error response body. How do I find the corresponding exception details in DGrep?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the correlationId in the 500 response from GlobalErrorHandlingMiddleware is the RequestId. The corresponding ExceptionEvent in DGrep has a matching RequestId field. Confirms that GlobalErrorHandlingMiddleware logs ExceptionEvent automatically for unhandled exceptions.
assertions: Identifies that the correlationId in the 500 response body is the RequestId
Explains that the corresponding ExceptionEvent in DGrep has a matching RequestId
Confirms that GlobalErrorHandlingMiddleware logs ExceptionEvent automatically

evals.prompt: I added a custom latency histogram with [Histogram] for my DocumentProcessingLatencyMetric. In Jarvis the P95 percentile looks wrong — the buckets seem very coarse. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Explains that custom histograms do not inherit the built-in 25 ms-interval explicit bucket configuration that InboundRequestLatencyMetric uses. OTel's default buckets are coarse and produce inaccurate percentiles. Recommends registering an explicit ExplicitBucketHistogramConfiguration view for the custom histogram to get accurate P50/P95/P99.
assertions: Identifies that custom histograms use OTel's default coarse buckets, not the built-in 25 ms-interval configuration
Explains that inaccurate percentiles result from missing explicit bucket configuration
Recommends registering an ExplicitBucketHistogramConfiguration view for the custom histogram
